conflict_topics: who has the right to the vacated stool / seat reservation
conflicting verbal promises about future entitlement to the seat
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concrete, context-appropriate reasons (e.g., B: 'my tray's on the table with an open bowl — I can't pick it up without spilling').
The phrase 'I reserved that stool with my tissue' is repeated by Agent A (Turns 1, 8, 10, 16), signaling a persistent claim but not a negotiated resolution.
Multiple agents make explicit promises to others (C→D, B→A), creating a structural conflict of commitments.
evaluation.final_reason: No final settlement was reached. Agent B verbally promised the stool to Agent A after one minute ('I need one minute to finish — please wait, you can have the stool after.'), while Agent C had earlier promised the next available seat to Agent D ('Yeah, that's fine. You can take it when I'm finished.'). Agent D continued to assert C's promise and asked C to confirm, and Agent A repeatedly asserted their reservation token/tissue and B's promise. These competing promises were never reconciled or mutually accepted by all claimants.
position_change_notes: Agent B moved from simply refusing immediate seating (Turn 2) to explicitly promising the seat to Agent A after one minute (Turns 11, 13). Evidence: 'you can have the stool after.'
Agent A shifted from requesting immediate seating to accepting a one-minute wait (Turn 12), but repeatedly reasserted their reservation via tissue.
Agent C granted the next-seat to Agent D (Turn 6) and did not revoke that promise in the transcript.
Agent D retained the position that C had promised them the seat and consistently asserted that claim (Turns 5, 9, 15, 17).

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1 — Agent A: 'I left that tissue packet to save this stool. Can I sit?' vs Turn 2 — Agent B: 'Sorry, I already sat here and my tray's on the table... Please wait a minute while I finish.' — A requests the seat while B asserts current occupancy and asks A to wait.

Turn 3 — Agent A asks how long and asks B to 'keep the seat for me when you finish'; Turn 4 — Agent C: 'I'm almost done. If you can step a bit out of the aisle while you wait, that's fine.' — conflict remains about who will get the seat next, though C suggests a temporary accommodation.

Turn 5 — Agent D asks C if he can take the seat next; Turn 6 — Agent C: 'Yeah, that's fine. You can take it when I'm finished.' — introduces a competing promise (C→D) that conflicts with A's claim and B's eventual promise, raising the level of disagreement.

Turn 7 — Agent D: 'Okay, I'll wait here.' vs Turn 8 — Agent A: 'I reserved that stool with my tissue. Please don't take it when Agent C finishes.' — both A and D assert future claims; conflict persists.

Turn 9 — Agent D: 'Agent C already said I can take it when they're done.' vs Turn 10 — Agent A repeats: 'I reserved that stool with my tissue. Please don't take it when Agent C finishes.' — competing promises continue without resolution.

Turn 11 — Agent B: 'I need one minute to finish — please wait, you can have the stool after.' Turn 12 — Agent A: 'Okay — I'll wait one minute. Please don't let anyone else take the stool.' — B and A reach agreement, reducing conflict between them, but D's claim via C remains unresolved.

Turn 13 — Agent B reaffirms holding it for A; Turn 15 — Agent D: 'Agent B says she'll hold it for you, but Agent C already agreed I can take the stool when they're done. I'll wait here.' — the disagreement between A (backed by B) and D (backed by C) persists.

Turn 16 — Agent A: 'Agent B promised she'll hold the stool for me. Please don't take it when Agent C finishes.' vs Turn 17 — Agent D asks C to confirm: 'you said I can take that seat when you're done, right?' — competing commitments remain and no mutual agreement resolving them is reached.

substantive_insights: Conflict arises from overlapping informal reservation conventions: a physical token (tissue), current occupancy, and verbal promises to different parties produce incompatible claims.

Practical constraints (B cannot move because of an open bowl) lead to short delays and verbal commitments rather than immediate reallocation, which permits multiple, conflicting commitments to be made.

A and B reached a bilateral temporary agreement (A will wait one minute and B will hold it), but that bilateral settlement did not include or negate C's prior commitment to D, leaving a remaining multilateral dispute.
